report_html:
A Ground-First Machine

The backfield runs through one man — their top back absorbs 76% of the carries (league ~59%), a true bell-cow share that makes his rushing volume among the safest floors in the sport when the script cooperates.

The Offensive Blueprint

Few offenses are as committed to the run as BAL. Their pass rate over expected sits at -8% — well below the -2% norm — and it collapses to 30% once they're in front. The script writes itself: build a lead, then bludgeon.

Their run game attacks the perimeter — 33% of carries hit the edge (league ~25%), an outside-zone lean that rewards speed backs and can boom for chunk gains.

By the numbers it's an efficient unit — a 48% success rate (above the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is run-first (43% pass), funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — They Force the Throw

Soft against opposing WR1s — 74 rec yds/game (vs ~58). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 94 rushing and 257 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). They wall the run and force the throw — attack with the opposing WR room.

Soft against backs out of the backfield — 22 rec yds/game (vs ~18). A rec-yards target.

A stingy, efficient defense — just 42% success allowed (vs ~44%); temper expectations for opposing skill players.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; opposing WR1/WR2 are the target — this D forces the throw.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
